::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 9th 1882  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

Dear [Mr Duncan](people/person_448.qmd)

I send you a first instalment of the first book of [Historical poetry](cmy_books/cmybook_156.qmd),[^1] I think there are about 30 of such pieces as these, containing nothing too difficult for a child of nine or eight years old. I suppose that will be enough for the first book, as it would be better to have it small and cheap enough for being learnt at home.

I have chosen only what are simple in language and ideas. Some are written on purpose, and some I have altered.

Those for the second set are much easier to find, and I think there will be more of them, but I suppose that 40 should be about the number

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Endorsed: ‘Miss Yonge/ sends/ 1st Instalment/of/Ballad Book/Part I/13/6/82’.
[^2]: Duncan was the secretary of the [National Society](organizations/other_32.qmd), the publishers of *Historical Ballads*.
